title: Blood test from a vein
what: A nurse takes a small amount of blood from a vein in your arm with a thin needle. One tube of blood can be used for many tests.
why: For blood chemistry, hormones, infections, clotting, and most other blood tests.
tell_doctor: If you have ever felt faint or passed out during a blood test
If you are allergic to latex or medical tape

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: For many tests, you need to fast for 8 to 12 hours. Plain water is fine. Ask the lab what your tests need.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: For one day before, avoid alcohol and hard workouts. Try not to smoke in the morning.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. If you take medicines in the morning, ask your doctor whether to take them before or after the test.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear a sleeve that rolls up easily above the elbow.

bring: Your test request form or list of tests
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tied above your elbow and you are asked to make a fist a few times
The skin is cleaned with antiseptic
A quick prick: the needle stays in the vein for a few seconds while blood fills the tubes
The band and needle are removed, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse and you can lie down
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes and keep your arm straight
A small bruise can happen and goes away on its own
Results usually take 1 to 3 days. The lab will tell you when
red_flags: The spot is very swollen, painful, and red
Numbness or strong pain in the arm

faq.q: Can I drink water before a blood test?
faq.a: Yes, plain still water is fine. If you need to fast, skip tea, coffee, and juice.

faq.q: Why do I feel dizzy after a blood test?
faq.a: It can happen from nerves or hunger. Sit for a while, drink some water, and eat something sweet.

reminders.text: Blood test tomorrow. If you need to fast, do not eat after dinner. Water is fine.
